text:
Alex: FYI — overnight canary in eu-west-1 started failing provisioning at ~02:10 UTC. noticed a pattern: BMC logs show IPMI lease expiry, then some nodes flipped boot order to PXE instead of local disk. GPUs ended up offline for k8s provisioning :grimace:

Sophia: :eyes: which pool? how many nodes impacted? any obvious firmware version skew?

Alex: ~23 nodes in gpu-pool-eu-west (mixed A100/V100). firmware reported as 2.1.8/2.1.9 across the set. logs from one host:```
[2026-03-19T02:09:57Z] ipmi: lease expired, renewing
[2026-03-19T02:10:01Z] bmc: set_bootdev pxe
[2026-03-19T02:10:02Z] system: reboot requested by bmc (watchdog)
[2026-03-19T02:10:20Z] bios: secureboot state: enabled -> default
```

Raj: that's nasty. could be a BMC watchdog/lease-turnover that applies a fallback boot setting. we saw something similar with an older provider SKU months ago. is there a common PSU swap or power event?

Alex: no power events in telemetry. rack-level PDUs stable. only thing correlating is ipmisession timer on our OOB proxy logs showing lease TTL hit then proxy reauth.

Lia: deploy-bot shows a firmware-flash job yesterday targeting same rack but used the non-idempotent path (legacy-flash). might have left some BMCs in a weird state. deploy-bot: ``job/firmware/2026-03-18-22:14:00 started``

deploy-bot: job/firmware/2026-03-18-22:14:00 completed with warnings on 7 hosts (watchdog-reset observed)

Sam: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) drain affected nodes from scheduler 2) set boot order back to disk via IPMI/Redfish 3) hold running canary rollout and rollback the firmware job. I can run `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U root -P $PASS chassis bootdev disk` in batches of 5.

Sophia: agree. also create alert for ``oob.boot_order_change`` with severity P1 until we patch runbooks. we lost ~2.5k GPU-hours in the stall window — costy.

Raj: small script to revert boot and check secureboot state:```
for bmc in $(cat /tmp/bmc-list); do
  ipmitool -I lanplus -H $bmc -U admin -P $PASS chassis bootdev disk || echo "$bmc fail"
  ssh oob@$bmc 'hexdump -C /sys/firmware/efi/vars/SecBoot* 2>/dev/null || true'
done
```

Lia: i'll pull the BMC proxy logs and look for session churn + cert expiry. also verifying that KMS rotation didn't touch any HSM-backed boot vars.

Alex: action plan:
- Sam to run bootstrap revert in 5-node batches, mark nodes drained (in progress)
- Lia to triage proxy TTL churn + correlate with firmware job outputs (ETA 30m)
- Raj to open a rollback on the firmware job and block further flashes until runbook updated
- Sophia to create a short-lived P1 alert for boot-order flips and add `oob.boot_order_change` metric ingestion point

Sam: started batch-1 (bmc-list batch 1): 5 nodes, 4 succeeded, 1 returned timeout. continuing.

Alex: note — one host's BIOS snapped secureboot back to default on reboot which requires re-enrollment of the platform key if we want to keep secureboot enforced. suggests the flash touched NVRAM.

Raj: we should avoid re-enrolling unattended unless we have the right key rotation logs. otherwise fallback is disable secureboot on affected nodes and treat them as transiently untrusted until full verification.

Sophia: risk/cost question: keep nodes offline longer to fully verify NVRAM vs. bring them back with secureboot disabled and reimage. which is faster?

Lia: reimage with secureboot off is faster (minutes per node) but has a security implication for customers on Dedicated/Private. need an approval from security for mass temporary disable.

Alex: +1 on a conservative approach. for now, we will: complete reverts, reimage affected nodes with secureboot disabled, patch the firmware job and proxy TTL, then do a controlled re-enroll of platform keys in a later maintenance window.

Sam: batch-3 done. drained + rebooted 15/23 nodes. remaining 8 are timing out on IPMI (proxy reauth loop).

Lia: found proxy churn logs: our OOB proxy had a cert auto-rotation at 02:05 that triggered re-auth for sessions older than 30m. the proxy client retries causing transient IPMI lease reset which trips some BMC fallback to PXE. opening PR to keep sessions sticky across cert rotation.

Raj: please capture a short runbook update: add step to set `bootdev disk persistent` after reflash and verify `secureboot` variable presence. also add pre-flight to ensure proxy cert rotation is rolling (not global).

Sophia: i'll update the incident board and tag support/ops and security. adding cost note: estimated 2.5k GPU-hours * $X = ~$Y (tbd) for finance follow-up.

Alex: thanks all. i'll follow up with a postmortem once we have logs + firmware job rollback confirmed. short-term: blocked further firmware pushes to that rack and flagged the rack in inventory as "oob-risk". :white_check_mark:
